chunks: From him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a free man: does he make a slave woman lawful for himself (through marriage)? He said: 'A free man does not make a slave woman lawful, nor does a slave woman make a free man lawful. And a Jew makes a Christian woman lawful, and a Christian makes a Jewess lawful.'

key_terms.الْحُرِّ: The free man (one who is not a slave)
key_terms.يُحْصِنُ: To make lawful (specifically through marriage contract)

ai.seo_question: Can a free man marry a slave woman in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the specific restrictions of *ihdan* (marriage that confers full marital rights) by distinguishing between social status and religious affiliation. While a free man cannot fully marry a slave woman (and vice versa) due to the disparity in their legal standing, Jews and Christians are permitted to marry each other, demonstrating that the prohibition is not based on interfaith barriers but on the free/slave hierarchy. This ruling highlights the nuanced Shia jurisprudence regarding the conditions of valid marriage contracts in early Islamic society.
